literal.prompt: На карте движения ледникового щита видны медленные области у пологой вершины и быстрые полосы, ведущие к отдельным выходным ледникам. Как называется внутренний рубеж между бассейнами, из которых лёд направляется к разным выходам?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L102-L104 gives the ice-sheet flow pattern: slow near the shallow summit, outward to faster coastal outlet glaciers. Glossary L58-L64 identifies the internal divide. The options are related flow-map features but distinguish boundary, fast ribbon, coastal outlet, and grounded-to-floating transition.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Ice Sheets L102-L105: ice flows outward from the center; near summit slow, faster toward coastal outlets; ice streams are fast ribbons bounded by slower ice; outlets carry ice to ocean and may become floating shelf. NSIDC Cryosphere Glossary L58-L64: ice divide separates opposing flow directions on a glacier or ice sheet. NASA Landsat L263: grounded ice detaches from seafloor and floats at the grounding line.

literalGroups.literal: Это ледораздел: NSIDC определяет его как границу между областями с противоположными направлениями движения льда. На щите он отделяет внутренние бассейны, лёд из которых направляется к разным выходным ледникам.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The glossary defines ice divide as a boundary separating opposite ice-flow directions (L58-L64); the ice-sheet page gives the outward-flow and outlet-glacier context (L102-L105).
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Cryosphere Glossary L58-L64: ice divide separates opposing flow directions on a glacier or ice sheet. NSIDC Ice Sheets L102-L105: ice flows outward from the center; near summit slow, faster toward coastal outlets; ice streams are fast ribbons bounded by slower ice; outlets carry ice to ocean and may become floating shelf.

literalGroups.literal: На линии налегания наземный лёд теряет опору на морском дне и переходит в плавучий шельф.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA L263 defines the grounding line transition where grounded continental ice detaches from seafloor and floats.
literalGroups.locator: NASA Landsat L263: grounded ice detaches from seafloor and floats at the grounding line.

literalGroups.literal: Ледораздел бывает как на ледниковом щите, так и на отдельном леднике.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L58-L60 applies the term to a glacier or an ice sheet; the note adds individual glaciers beyond the prompt setting.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Cryosphere Glossary L58-L64: ice divide separates opposing flow directions on a glacier or ice sheet.

literalGroups.literal: Ледниковые потоки — длинные полосы быстро движущегося льда, окружённые более медленным льдом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L105 describes ice streams as long ribbons of fast-flowing ice bounded by slower-moving ice.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Ice Sheets L102-L105: ice flows outward from the center; near summit slow, faster toward coastal outlets; ice streams are fast ribbons bounded by slower ice; outlets carry ice to ocean and may become floating shelf.

literalGroups.literal: Выходные ледники переносят лёд щита к морю; у побережья он может стать плавучим шельфом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L104-L105 says outlet glaciers move ice to the ocean and ice may become a floating shelf.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Ice Sheets L102-L105: ice flows outward from the center; near summit slow, faster toward coastal outlets; ice streams are fast ribbons bounded by slower ice; outlets carry ice to ocean and may become floating shelf.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Russian-speaking adults familiar with basic glacier/ice-sheet dynamics.
absoluteDifficulty.ground: The prompt no longer repeats the keyed definition or its lexical components. It requires using the topical flow pattern of a sheet—slow near the summit, outward movement, and fast coastal outlets—to identify the interior basin boundary among several related flow features. This is lower-end medium application, not broad-adult recall; the alternatives are all glaciological flow/boundary structures rather than unrelated objects.
